body:
Just doing some blind reading (don't know much c++)

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp#L913 

Could it be this area? Where there's no check for other filters or else to the mipmap? Unless I'm missing something this would always default to linear or linear w/ mipmaps.

> Just doing some blind reading (don't know much c++)
> 
> [godot/servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp#L913)
> 
> Line 913 in [45fc515](/godotengine/godot/commit/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b)
> 
>  if (u.filter >= ShaderLanguage::FILTER_NEAREST_MIPMAP) { 
> Could it be this area? Where there's no check for other filters or else to the mipmap? Unless I'm missing something this would always default to linear or linear w/ mipmaps.

I don't think this is the cause. That's shared code between all the renderers, so if it failed here, it would also be failing in Vulkan. And this isn't related to mipmaps either.

The code for updating the texture filter in GL appears to be here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/825ef2387f87de1c350696886e6c50b039204cef/drivers/gles3/storage/material_storage.cpp#L2727

The problem is that this code relies on texture uniform data, which isn't generated for screen read textures:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/825ef2387f87de1c350696886e6c50b039204cef/drivers/gles3/storage/material_storage.cpp#L852-L856

Is there a reason why we're doing this? How else can we get the necessary information to the GLES canvas rendering code?
